subject: Architecture
title: Cambodian Temple Cosmology: Angkor Wat's Hidden Map
description: A quick win: understand Cambodian Temple Cosmology: Angkor Wat's Hidden Map.

hook.text: Angkor Wat isn't just a temple — it's a scale model of the Hindu universe carved in stone.

buildup.text: Five towers represent Mount Meru's peaks. The moat represents the cosmic ocean surrounding the world.

discovery.text: The temple is oriented to the west — unusual for Hindu temples — possibly representing the setting sun and death.

twist.text: During the spring equinox, the sun rises directly over the central tower — a precision alignment from 1150 AD.

climax.text: Angkor Wat's bas-reliefs span 2,600 feet — depicting gods, battles, and the entire Hindu creation myth.

punchline.text: They didn't just build a temple. They built the universe.

quiz.question: What does Angkor Wat's moat represent?
options: The Mekong River that sustained the Khmer Empire
The cosmic ocean surrounding the Hindu universe
A defensive barrier against invading armies

details.summary: Angkor Wat, built in the early 12th century by King Suryavarman II, is a 162-hectare temple complex that functions as a three-dimensional map of Hindu cosmology.
details.whyItMatters: Angkor Wat proves that an entire landscape can become sacred architecture. The temple doesn't merely represent the cosmos — at 162 hectares, it replicates the cosmos at city scale.
takeaways: 162-hectare complex is a three-dimensional map of Hindu cosmology
Five towers represent Mount Meru's peaks, the moat the cosmic ocean
Bas-reliefs depict mythological narratives across hundreds of meters

faq.question: How big is Angkor Wat compared to other temples?
faq.answer: Angkor Wat covers 162 hectares — the largest religious monument ever built. For comparison, Vatican City is 44 hectares. The surrounding moat alone is 1.5 km by 1.3 km wide. The outer gallery walls contain nearly 600 meters of continuous bas-relief sculpture.

faq.question: Why does Angkor Wat face west instead of east like most Hindu temples?
faq.answer: Most scholars believe the westward orientation relates to Vishnu, the temple's presiding deity, whose direction is west. Others suggest it functioned as a funerary temple for Suryavarman II. The western orientation means the temple is spectacularly lit by the rising sun behind it at equinox.
